newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine approves privatisation of 37 large firms.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine approves privatisation of 37 large firms.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has approved privatisation of 37 large enterprises through direct foreign investment, the deputy prime minister in charge of the economy said on Wednesday.
"Yesterday the Cabinet of Ministers met and approved the majority of privatisation plans put forward," Viktor Pynzenyk told Reuters.
Pynzenyk, who did not specify the types of firms, said the government planned to privatise them through direct investment rather than privatisation certificates.

Four or five privatisation plans were set aside for further research, he said, including carmaker AvtoZAZ, the subject of investor interest by U.S. carmaker General Motors and South Korea's Daewoo Group. Yuri Yekhanurov, chief of the State Property Fund (FDM), the state privatisation agency, said a decision on privatising the country's largest alumina plant Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ) was also delayed.

Ukraine plans to sell no less than 70 percent shares in 3,000 large- and medium-scale enterprises this year, and an FDM official said previously it hopes to raise 500 million hryvnia from privatisation in 1997.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in private foreign investment since independence in 1991.
Parliament is due to review this year's privatisation programme next month.
A decision on AvtoZAZ plant, located in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhya, is also due next month. The FDM is awaiting approval to sell 26 percent shares in MHZ.
